title.en: Closed-flux and magnetic-axis material support classification
title.zh: 闭合磁通面与磁轴材料支撑分类

summary: Classify which points of a solver grid carry cold-plasma material support from the poloidal flux already sampled on that grid, the cylindrical coordinates of the grid, the separatrix flux and the selected flux-surface side, the PML frame thickness, and the caller-owned PEC mask.

identity.relation: a sampled poloidal flux, the cylindrical coordinates of the sampling grid, a separatrix flux with a selected side, a PML frame thickness, and a PEC mask to the set of grid points with cold-plasma material support
identity.direction: poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad, covered_mask, radii_m, axial_coordinate_m, separatrix_flux_wb_per_rad, closed_flux_side, xpoint_half_length_m, pml_cells, pec_mask -> material_support_mask, closed_flux_mask, axis_segment_mask
identity.definition: Forms the closed-flux mask as the covered points on the selected side of the separatrix flux, forms the innermost-radius segment as the covered points at the grid's minimum radius within the poloidal half length, excludes the PML frame on all six faces of the solver box, excludes the caller's PEC mask, and requires the result to be non-empty.
identity.model: geometric material-support classification on a sampled flux surface; no plasma model, no field solve, and no flux-surface reconstruction is performed
identity.geometry: the flux surface is supplied as a sampled scalar field, so the classification is purely geometric in the sampled flux value and in the grid coordinates
identity.coordinates: cylindrical radius and axial coordinate of the sampling grid, together with the discrete index position of each point in the solver box
identity.boundary: the PML frame is the set of points within pml_cells of any of the six faces of the solver box; the frame thickness must be a positive integer, so a zero thickness is rejected rather than interpreted as an empty frame
assumptions: The poloidal flux was already sampled on the same grid, so no interpolation is performed here.
The coverage mask marks the points for which that sampling is defined; the classification never extends support beyond it.
The flux-surface side is a caller decision, so the relation never infers which side of the separatrix is confined.
The innermost radius present on the grid is the axis location; this coincides with the magnetic axis only when the grid actually contains r = 0.
The PEC mask is a caller-owned geometric declaration, not a derived quantity.

inputs.name: poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad
inputs.description: Poloidal flux per radian sampled on the solver grid.
inputs.constraints: Finite and three-dimensional. Non-finite flux is rejected, because a non-finite sample cannot be compared against the separatrix flux.

inputs.name: covered_mask
inputs.description: Points for which the flux sampling is defined.
inputs.constraints: Must match the flux shape. Support is never granted outside this mask.

inputs.name: radii_m
inputs.description: Cylindrical radius of every grid point.
inputs.constraints: Finite, non-negative, and matching the flux shape. The grid's minimum value locates the innermost radius.

inputs.name: axial_coordinate_m
inputs.description: Axial coordinate of every grid point.
inputs.constraints: Finite and matching the flux shape. Its absolute value is compared against the poloidal half length.

inputs.name: separatrix_flux_wb_per_rad
inputs.description: Poloidal flux per radian of the separatrix.
inputs.constraints: Finite. Not required to lie inside the sampled flux range; a separatrix outside the range simply makes the selected side empty, which then fails the non-empty support requirement.

inputs.name: closed_flux_side
inputs.description: Which side of the separatrix flux is confined.
inputs.constraints: Exactly 'less_than' or 'greater_than'. Any other value is rejected rather than defaulted.

inputs.name: xpoint_half_length_m
inputs.description: Poloidal half length around the midplane within which the innermost-radius segment counts as support.

inputs.name: pml_cells
inputs.description: Thickness of the perfectly matched layer frame, in grid cells, excluded on all six faces of the solver box.
inputs.constraints: A positive integer. A zero thickness is rejected: the retained relation expressed the exclusion as slice assignments, and a zero thickness made every slice cover the whole box.

inputs.name: pec_mask
inputs.constraints: Must match the flux shape. PEC points are removed from the support after the flux-surface classification.

outputs.name: material_support_mask
outputs.description: Grid points carrying cold-plasma material support.
outputs.constraints: Guaranteed non-empty: an empty mask raises instead of being returned, because a solve with no cold-plasma material is not a result of this relation.

outputs.name: closed_flux_mask
outputs.description: Covered grid points on the selected side of the separatrix flux, before the PML frame and the PEC mask are applied.
outputs.constraints: A subset of covered_mask. Returned so that a caller can attribute an empty or surprising support mask to the flux-surface choice rather than to the frame or the conductor mask.

outputs.name: axis_segment_mask
outputs.description: Covered grid points at the grid's innermost radius within the poloidal half length, before the PML frame and the PEC mask are applied.
outputs.constraints: A subset of covered_mask. Because the retained relation intersects this term with the coverage mask, it is empty whenever the sampled equilibrium's radial axis begins above the grid's minimum radius.

preconditions: The poloidal flux has already been sampled on the solver grid, and the coverage mask states where that sampling is defined.
The caller has decided which side of the separatrix flux is confined and the poloidal half length of interest.
The solver box has a genuine PML frame of at least one cell.
supported: Any PML frame thickness that leaves a non-empty interior.
The innermost-radius segment may add covered, non-PEC, non-PML points whether the minimum grid radius is zero or positive; for positive minimum radius it is a geometric proxy, not the magnetic axis.
PEC masks of any shape-compatible pattern.
excluded: Interpolation or reconstruction of the flux field; the flux must already be sampled.
Inferring which side of the separatrix is confined.
Identifying the magnetic axis from the flux field; the innermost-radius segment is a geometric proxy only.
Any plasma, collisionality, or wave model.
Solver grids with no PML frame, which are rejected rather than treated as having an empty frame.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when the flux is not a finite 3D array, when covered_mask, radii_m, axial_coordinate_m, or pec_mask does not match the flux shape, when radii_m is negative or non-finite, when the coordinate arrays are non-finite, when the separatrix flux is non-finite, when closed_flux_side is not one of the two allowed values, when the poloidal half length is non-finite or not strictly positive, or when pml_cells is not a positive integer.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the classified support mask is empty. The message names the closed-flux side, the innermost-radius segment, the PML frame, and the PEC mask as the contributing causes, rather than attributing the outcome to the equilibrium.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this relation is a fixed sequence of mask operations with no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no mapping.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel-owned split of the second of the two scientific relations that the retained coarse-CAD full-wave entry performed inside one operator. The retained operator also performed the cylindrical-to-Cartesian reconstruction and read the equilibrium map arrays; this relation reads neither, so the two are independent scientific identities and are proposed as separately reviewable assets. The retained relation expressed the PML exclusion as six slice assignments, and a frame thickness of zero made every one of those slices cover the whole solver box, so the mask was empty and the caller received an error blaming the machine equilibrium; the review diagnosed that defect and this asset replaces it with an explicit positive-integer precondition on pml_cells plus an empty-support error that names the real causes. That precondition is not a behavioural regression, because a zero thickness never produced a support mask in the retained route either. The review also established that the innermost-radius segment is intersected with the coverage mask, so it can only add points when the sampled equilibrium's radial axis begins at the grid's minimum radius; that interaction is preserved and documented rather than changed. The observation snapshot and the batch inventory are private review artifacts and are not part of the public contract.

python.signature: classify_material_support(poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad, covered_mask, radii_m, axial_coordinate_m, *, separatrix_flux_wb_per_rad, closed_flux_side, xpoint_half_length_m, pml_cells, pec_mask)

example.description: Classify material support on a 9x9x7 grid from a synthetic flux field, and check that the PML frame and the PEC mask both bite.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry import classify_material_support
x_m = np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 9)
y_m = np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 9)
z_m = np.linspace(-0.4, 0.4, 7)
xx, yy, zz = np.meshgrid(x_m, y_m, z_m, indexing='ij')
radii = np.hypot(xx, yy)
flux = 0.9 * radii + 0.1 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * zz)
covered = (radii >= 0.05) & (radii <= 1.0) & (zz >= -0.5) & (zz <= 0.5)
pec = np.zeros((9, 9, 7), dtype=bool)
pec[5, 5, 3] = True
result = classify_material_support(
    flux,
    covered,
    radii,
    zz,
    separatrix_flux_wb_per_rad=0.4,
    closed_flux_side='less_than',
    xpoint_half_length_m=0.2,
    pml_cells=1,
    pec_mask=pec,
)
support = result['material_support_mask']
assert support.dtype == bool and support.shape == (9, 9, 7)
assert support.sum() > 0
assert not support[0, :, :].any() and not support[-1, :, :].any()
assert not support[:, 0, :].any() and not support[:, -1, :].any()
assert not support[:, :, 0].any() and not support[:, :, -1].any()
assert not support[5, 5, 3]
assert not result['axis_segment_mask'].any()
assert result['closed_flux_mask'].sum() >= support.sum()
example.expected: A non-empty support mask with no support on any of the six solver-box faces, the PEC point excluded, and an empty innermost-radius segment because the flux axis starts above the grid's minimum radius.

scope: Both separatrix sides, their disjointness, and the monotonicity of the less_than side in the separatrix flux.
Exclusion of the PML frame on all six faces for two different frame thicknesses.
Removal of PEC points after the flux-surface classification.
The zero-thickness rejection, together with a demonstration that the retained route also never returned a mask for a zero thickness and that its error named the wrong cause.
The innermost-radius segment as a live branch, adding exactly the axis points on a side that excludes the axis, and as an inert branch when the coverage mask intersects it away.
The empty-support error naming the actual contributing causes.
Exact agreement with the retained support mask for the same sampled flux and coordinates.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes that the declared classification reproduces the retained support mask, that the zero-thickness defect is replaced by an explicit precondition, and that the innermost-radius segment's interaction with the coverage mask is preserved and documented. It does not establish that the selected side of the separatrix flux is physically the confined region for any device, nor that the innermost grid radius coincides with the magnetic axis.
known_limitations: The magnetic axis is identified with the grid's innermost radius, which is the grid's r = 0 only when the grid contains the origin. On a grid that does not, the axis term marks a thin column at the smallest sampled radius instead of the axis.

The innermost-radius segment is intersected with the coverage mask, so it cannot add points when the equilibrium map's radial axis begins above the grid's minimum radius. The retained relation behaves the same way, so this is preserved rather than repaired.
A solver grid with no PML frame is rejected rather than supported. A no-frame run is a different relation and would need its own asset.
The relation is purely geometric in the sampled flux; it does not verify that the sampled flux is a physical equilibrium.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
